# ZenFS Copilot Instructions

## Architecture & Key Concepts

- ZenFS centers on three layers: the internal API in src/internal, modular backends in src/backends, and the VFS/node emulation layer in src/vfs and src/node.
- src/index.ts wires the package exports, exposing the compat fs shim plus helper entry points (configure, mounts, vfs) for consumers.
- Configuration flows through configure/configureSingle/resolveMountConfig (src/config.ts), which resolve Backend objects into FileSystem instances and mount them via src/vfs/shared.ts.
- Context binding (src/context.ts) provides chroot-like scopes with cloned credentials from src/internal/credentials.ts; use it instead of manually mutating global state.
- Device handling uses DeviceFS from src/internal/devices.ts, enabled via the addDevices flag in configure; ensure /dev mounts stay consistent when tweaking device drivers.

## Source Layout

- src/internal/filesystem.ts, inode.ts, and index_fs.ts implement the core FileSystem contract every backend must fulfill; extend FileSystem rather than bypassing it.
- Built-in backends (memory, fetch, passthrough, port, single_buffer, cow, store) live under src/backends and re-exported through src/backends/index.ts.
- src/mixins contains composeable behaviors (Async, Mutexed, Readonly, Shared, Sync) that wrap FileSystem instances—reuse them for new backends.
- src/node holds Node.js compatibility shims (compat.ts, promises.ts, dir.ts, streams.ts); these mirror node:fs semantics and feed the public fs export.
- Ancillary definitions sit in types/ (ambient d.ts) and dist/ (tsc output shipped with the package); edit src/ and regenerate dist/ instead of touching dist/ directly.

## Build & Tooling

- TypeScript uses NodeNext module resolution; keep relative imports with explicit .js extensions and favor named exports to avoid dual-mode issues.
- Run npm run build (or npx tsc) to refresh dist/ after TypeScript edits; npm run dev starts tsc --watch for iterative work.
- npm run lint enforces eslint.config.js and npm run format:check validates Prettier settings (tabs + trailing commas); fix before committing.
- Scripts under scripts/ follow the parseArgs/styleText pattern (see scripts/test.js, scripts/make-index.js); match that style for new CLIs.
- Preserve the SPDX header (// SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-3.0-or-later) at the top of new source and test files.

## Tests

- npm test invokes scripts/test.js, which handles coverage (via c8), runs Node test suites from tests/fs, and executes tests/fetch/run.sh for fetch backend checks.
- Tests require a built dist/; pass -b or run npm run build beforehand to avoid the "Missing build" guard in scripts/test.js.
- Each backend harness in tests/setup/\*.ts calls configureSingle to mount the target FileSystem; SETUP env var selects one when zenfs-test iterates.
- Shared helpers live in tests/common.ts and tests/setup.ts, copying fixtures from tests/data into the virtual FS; reuse copySync/copyAsync helpers instead of rolling bespoke setup.
- Use npx zenfs-test --help for focused runs (e.g. npx zenfs-test -ac tests/setup/memory.ts to run common + memory suites) and --report/--clean to manage coverage artifacts.

## Conventions & Patterns

- Follow CONTRIBUTING.md guidance: prefer guard clauses over deep nesting, avoid single-letter or abbreviated identifiers, and document non-obvious units in comments.
- Rely on kerium logging and withErrno for error paths (see src/config.ts, src/backends/cow.ts) instead of raw Error/console usage.
- When adding backends, validate options through checkOptions (src/backends/backend.ts) and export the backend from src/backends/index.ts so consumers can import it.
- Mount mutations should go through mount/umount from src/vfs/shared.ts; keep mounts map coherent with global state (globalThis.**zenfs** is updated in src/index.ts).
- Store-based backends expect indexes generated by scripts/make-index.js; regenerate fixtures when adjusting src/backends/store/\* behavior to keep tests deterministic.
